$comment: OBRA Level 2 dialogue. RULE: no line may name a drawable class -- checked word-boundary against all 50 ids AND display names. This level's vocabulary is unusually dangerous: the plaza is a SQUARE, the palms are TREES, the lit house has a DOOR, the offering is BREAD, the sky has a SUN and CLOUDS, and the birds are BIRDS. Every one of those is a class. They are phrased around: 'the plaza', 'the palms', 'the light in the window', 'something to eat', 'the light', 'the flock'. Tags appear in exactly one surface form, marked with **.

lines.text: She painted this from the church steps, apo. Same hour, same heat.
The whole town is out. And her next one is here somewhere — in pieces. They did not walk off.
See the fold, apo? Right through her plaza. That was us. That was a thing we did.
Two things. One: whatever you become, keep it under the strings. They will not move for you.
Two: nothing small. A hundred feet on this ground today, and nobody looking down.
Hoy! I told you. Under the strings.
Naku. Come here. You are going to get yourself stepped on.
Not that one, apo. Too small for today. Pick something the crowd will see.
The church first. She never came empty-handed — always a light to leave burning.
We have nothing to leave. So we get one. The plaza is full of people who have it.
Three ways, and one is not drawing. Ask the dancers. They will want something back.
Or the houses. One has a light in the window, and something that can **unlock** gets you in.
Or clear them out. Something that can **startle** — big enough a crowd does not argue.
So. How are we getting it?

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: I will dance for them.
Ha! Your lola danced that badly the first time too. They still gave her the flower.
Naku. You have your lola's feet. Go on — they are still waiting.
Never mind, apo. You have what we came for. Keep your feet — that is the important part.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.choice_label: Someone is home. I will let myself in.
lines.text: Someone is home. I will let myself in.
We have done this before, you and I. You are faster now.
Take it and leave something on the sill. We are borrowing, not taking.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: I will clear the plaza.
Apo. If you do this they will not come back. Not today, not for us.
It is very quiet now. She painted this plaza full, apo.
Good. Inside, then. Wipe your feet.
Light it, apo, and set it on the rack. Not the middle — she always went to the left, nearer the wall.
There. Let it burn for her a while.

lines.speaker: priest
lines.text: You lit one for her? She was here this morning. That same rack, then the pew by the wall, for a long while.

lines.speaker: priest
lines.text: When she got up she did not go out the front. She went out the back, through there, into the alleys behind the plaza.

lines.speaker: priest
lines.text: Two narrow ways, one after the other, and dark even now. Something back there has been nesting in the bunting.
There. Look up. Five of them, and every one has a piece of her in its beak.
They are not stealing, apo. They are nesting — up in the strings, all of them.
Three ways again. Bring them down gently — something that can **feed**, set down where they can see it.
Or go up after the nests — something that can **climb**, then something that can **cut**. Down come the strings, and they let go.
Or knock them out of the air. Something that can **strike**, thrown. They will not come to you.
So. How do we get her back?

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: I will feed them.
Every morning, apo. She said they were the only ones who waited for her.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.choice_label: I will cut their nests down.
lines.text: I will cut their nests down.
Up you go, then. Cut the strings from up there.
There goes the bunting. They will string it up again. They always do.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: I will knock them down.
That is the last of them. Poor things — they were only nesting.
Two more, apo. The last of her.
Look how late it has got. She would be packing up her brushes by now.
Same three ways. Something that can **feed**, and they come down to it.
Something that can **climb**, then something that can **cut**, and the strings come down.
Or something that can **strike**, and a good arm.
Your hands, apo. Not mine.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.choice_label: I will feed these two as well.
lines.text: I will feed these two as well.
Slow, and everything still standing. She would have done it that way and complained.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.choice_label: I will bring these strings down too.
lines.text: I will bring these strings down too.
Up again. Mind the flags on the way.
They put those up at first light, apo. All of them, together. It took the morning.
Well. The sky is open now, at least. Nothing left to be in anyone's way.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.choice_label: I will knock these two down.
lines.text: I will knock these two down.
There. Every piece of her. The table is through there, apo — come.
Lay them out. Corners first — she taught me that and I never once did it.
Water. Not this plaza at all, apo — the one she painted after it.
She painted that from a boat, and she could not swim. That is where we go next. Come.
I cannot read it, apo. That is my eyes, not your hand — draw it bigger and slower.
There. Now I see it.
Welcome back to the fiesta, apo! The drums never stopped while you were gone.
Back in the plaza. Listen — they are still singing.
You again! At this rate the dancers will teach you the steps.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: I already know two steps forward.
Then you only need the one step back.
Back from the terraces? You still have mud on your heels, apo.
Nobody here will notice. Everybody is too busy dancing.
You smell like the sea, apo! The plaza missed you.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: Is that seaweed in my hair?
Leave it. Call it a fiesta decoration.
Last time you danced your way through. She would have joined you.
Will you try another way today? The plaza has more than one way in.
Last time you let yourself in where you were not asked. Quick hands, apo.
Perhaps today, ask the town for help instead.
Last time you cleared a path through all of it. Strong, but loud.
Try something gentler today. It is a fiesta, after all.
She painted this fiesta like the Sinulog of Cebu. Every third Sunday of January, the whole city dances for the Santo Niño.
Sinulog comes from 'sulog' — the current of the water. Two steps forward, one step back, so the dance moves like a river.
When the drums are loudest, everyone shouts 'Pit Señor!' It means calling out to the Lord, asking Him to hear you.
The Santo Niño of Cebu was a gift to Queen Juana in 1521. It is the oldest Christian image in the Philippines.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: The old one, apo? Older than the church?
Older than every church here. They built the Basilica around it.
Four of our old churches — in Manila, Paoay, Santa Maria and Miagao — are UNESCO World Heritage Sites. The Baroque Churches of the Philippines.
See how thick those church walls are? Builders here made them wide and heavy, with great buttresses, so earthquakes could not knock them over.
People call it Earthquake Baroque. The ground here moves, so the churches learned to stand their ground.
San Agustin in Manila is the oldest stone church in the country. It has stood since 1607 — through earthquakes, fires and wars.
Every town in the Philippines keeps a fiesta for its patron saint. Houses open their tables, and even strangers are fed.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: Strangers too?
Especially strangers. Nobody walks home hungry from a fiesta.
Last time you danced for it. Will you try another way today?
Last time you let yourself into someone's house. Perhaps a kinder way, this time?
Last time you cleared the whole plaza. Gentler, this time?
You have tried every way here. Choose whichever you liked best.
Last time you fed them. There are other ways to get her pieces back.
Last time you cut their nests down. Will you try something else?
Last time you knocked them down. Perhaps something softer today?
Every way up to them, you have tried. Pick the one that felt right.
Last time you fed these two as well. Try another way?
Last time you brought their strings down. There is more than one way.
Last time you knocked these two down. Gentler, today?
You know every way to the last of her now. Choose what your heart says.
